newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks soft, but Germany at record high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks soft, but Germany at record high.

text.p: European bourses started weaker on Tuesday morning after Wall Street snapped its three-day winning streak overnight but German shares bucked the trend to score a record high.
The dollar edged up against the mark and yen, while gold steadied near its 12-year low on physical demand in Asia and the Middle East.
But traders did not expect gold's near-term stability to last. They said gold remained vulnerable to testing Monday's New York low of $314 per ounce.
The dollar's strength continued to lift German export shares, which led the 30-share DAX index up to an all-time high at the start of bourse trade.
Siemens AG was also among the winners, hitting a year high, in Frankfurt after Britain's General Electric Co Plc said it was reviewing its GPT telecoms joint venture with Siemens.
At 0850 GMT, Siemens was up 1.25 marks at 109.90, just off its year high of 110.10 set early in the day.
